title: A letter inviting his band to play a colored club
summary: A funny letter from a Black club asking his WWL-broadcasting band to play a dance, which never happened.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You could have hired Jack Lane's band.

Oh I didn't know man. I had the letter here. If I could find that letter and let you read that letter. It was really funny man. It had the funnies in that. Surgeys and Wilder. I knew it was a colored club though. But the man sure wrote a nice letter and said, how much you like the band. You know, we, we were playing out here at that time. I got that letter out there. I used to broadcast over at WWL a whole lot. You know. And, uh. He wanted us to come up there and play, play that dance. But. Never did get to make that one though. But I believe I, uh, uh, uh. Would have liked of playing it. I don't know. I don't think I'd have got a kick out of that. Yeah. I'd really believe so. I'd have got a kick out of that. I could have, could have got by with it. But. Never did get up there. Well let me ask you something. Yeah. Did any of your family play music? Well, uh. No, my, my, uh.
